reason: Idea sits well below grade 12: the whole insight is 'The red arrows. Warm water. The blue ones are cold.', with no competing values or abstraction.
Core insight is middle-school level ('So greenhouse gases are a blanket, not a villain') with jokey banter, and 'That's the chicanery' misuses the required word.
Plot loses track of its own numbers ('Twelve hundred,' then 'so I said 36 grams of water', with 36 g of hydrogen giving '18'), which makes the central insight confusing.
Thinking reads well below grade 12: the central insight is learning to read a shelf tag ('Unit price... Cost per gram'), with only a brief closing nod to anything abstract.
Reads young for grade 12: a peer tutors a sandwich analogy ('Whatever runs out first is what caps the product') with a neat resolution and no competing values.

Plot loses track: a freshly cut cereal-box strip bears the grandfather's scorecard and 'placement exam, failed, retake granted', and 'six months of knowing the answer' contradicts the days-long timeline.
Central scene contradicts itself: 'You did the complement backwards', yet the rewrite produces the same strand, 'CTAATGT again', which muddles the lesson.
Plot slip and thin ideas for grade 12: 'Their sister's moods were mercurial... but Danny had always thought Chloe's were worse' confuses who is who, and the thinking stays at concrete bead-threading.

Story loses track of its own facts: the 18-year-old won a contest 'Three years earlier, in fifth grade' 'even at ten', and the Alvarez scene ('turned out the way Mr. Alvarez always did') is garbled and goes nowhere.
Tangled plot: a POV jump to the counselor reveals 'the withdrawal from the private college... logged in August' for a student still in class, a subplot that is never resolved.
Plot contradicts itself: the NULL first yields 'four names', then the rerun 'with the blank still in place' yields 'nothing at all', which leaves the mechanism muddled; 'suture' is also forced.
Plot contradicts its own central problem: 'Maxime kept getting thirty-six' then 'Thirty-eight, again... thirty-eight was what his own arithmetic kept insisting.'
Plot loses its own timeline: he is already at the rehearsal, then 'I got back to the annex at two, exactly as I'd promised Priya I would, only two hours later than she'd expected me.'
Reads middle-school: plain short exchanges ('Fine. RNA polymerase.' 'She tried.') and a library-copy analogy with no abstract principle or competing values for grade 12.
Timeline contradicts itself: 'the workshop was tomorrow at nine' vs 'two days before he had to explain consent' vs 'Friday morning', and a high-schooler 'rehearsing, in his dorm room'.
Ending loses track of events: Dana 'did the aquifer thing yesterday', then 'No, mine was the football match... I did the film festival instead.'
Corrupted foreign-script text breaks a sentence: 'pulling the失败的 batch toward the edge of the table'.

The plot loses track of its characters: Priya speaks of herself in the third person ('Mrs. Trujillo circled mine the first time and Priya fixed it after,' Priya said), and the math teacher is 'he', then Mrs. Trujillo, then the debate coach.
Contradicts its own lesson that only nouns are capitalized: 'bellicose, which Levi at first misread as a place name because it was capitalized... it could not be a noun if it mattered where it sat'.
